title: How do we tile a grid when one side is even and one is odd?
description: A grid with m rows and n columns, where one of m and n is even and the other is odd. Upright tiles fill the columns when the rows are even, and lying tiles fill the rows when the columns are even. Keeko's doubt, that one odd side spoils it, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: lay the tiles along the even side, so every line has an even number of squares. Watch for students who give up when one side is odd.

source: Is an m × n grid tileable with 2 × 1 tiles if one of m and n
video_script.why: The child finds a plan for a grid with one even side and one odd side, whichever side is the even one.
video_script.substitution: Tiles go along the even side: vertical down even columns, or horizontal along even rows.
video_script.anchor: A grid of unit squares with m rows and n columns, where one of m and n is even and the other is odd, and a tile that covers 2 squares.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks one odd side spoils it. But only upright tiles were tried. Lying tiles along a row of even length also work.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, use vertical tiles down the even columns, or horizontal tiles along rows of even length.

final_answer.value: Yes: use vertical tiles along the even side's columns, or horizontal tiles along rows of even length
final_answer.spoken: yes, use vertical tiles down the even columns, or horizontal tiles along rows of even length

hold_back: horizontal tiles along rows of even length
maths_rules: If the number of rows m is even, cover each column with vertical tiles.
If instead the number of columns n is even, each row has an even number of squares.
Then cover each row with n ÷ 2 horizontal tiles.
Example: a 3 × 4 grid, each of the 3 rows takes 2 horizontal tiles, 6 tiles in all.
Slip: one odd side does not spoil the tiling; use the even side.
video_script.design: One general grid with one even side. The tiles go along that side, upright for even columns, lying for even rows. The slip is giving up at the odd side.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A grid has m rows and n columns. One of m and n is even, and the other is odd.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each tile covers two squares, and we may turn it.
Can the tiles cover every such grid, and what plan always works?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Covering a region with shapes, with no gaps and no overlaps, is called tiling.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>An m by n grid has m rows and n columns. The letters stand for any numbers.
